title: How your heart and lungs work together

steps.say: Your heart is a strong muscle about the size of your fist. It squeezes to pump blood around your body.

figure.alt: A heart and a pair of lungs.

steps.say: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry blood back to the heart.
steps.show: arteries go away, veins come back

steps.say: When you breathe in, air goes down your windpipe into your lungs. Oxygen passes from the air into your blood.
Your blood carries oxygen to every muscle. It brings carbon dioxide back to the lungs, and you breathe it out.
When you run, your muscles need more oxygen. Your heart beats faster and you breathe faster.

figure.alt: Bar chart: heart rate 80 beats per minute at rest and 145 after running.

steps.say: You can feel each heartbeat as a pulse in your wrist. Count the beats for one minute to find your pulse rate.

check.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood back to the heart?

options.why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
The lungs are where blood picks up oxygen. They are not blood vessels.

hints: There are two main kinds of blood vessel.
Remember that arteries carry blood away from the heart.
Cross out the choices that are not blood vessels.
check.explanation: Veins carry blood back to the heart. Arteries carry blood away from it.

check.prompt: Nadia counts 20 heartbeats in 15 seconds. What is her pulse rate in beats per minute?
hints: A pulse rate counts the beats in one whole minute.
A minute has four lots of 15 seconds.
check.explanation: 20 × 4 = 80, so her pulse rate is 80 beats per minute.
